project.name: CardDemo
project.description: AWS CardDemo migrated from z/OS COBOL, CICS, VSAM, JCL and BMS to Java 25 and Spring Boot

requireJavaVersion.message: Build with JDK 25 or newer: a lower JDK cannot compile release 25 sources.

requireMavenVersion.message: Requires Apache Maven 3.9.11 or newer. Use ./mvnw to get the pinned version.

requireReleaseDeps.message: No SNAPSHOT dependency may enter a reproducible build.

banDynamicVersions.message: Version ranges, LATEST and RELEASE are banned. Declare an exact version.

banDuplicatePomDependencyVersions.message: A dependency is declared twice. Remove the duplicate so its scope still applies.

requirePluginVersions.message: Every plugin must resolve to an exact version. Pin it in properties.

requireFilesExist.message: Coverage execution data is incomplete, so this build must not reach jacoco:merge. target/jacoco.exec is written by the unit tier at the test phase and target/jacoco-it.exec by the integration and end-to-end tiers at the integration-test phase; the file listed above is missing. Merging one of the two produces a report, and a 0.80 floor check, measured over half the evidence and reporting success - and the validation-gate evidence under target/gate-verification is then absent entirely, because the harness that writes it lives in the end-to-end tier. If a tier was skipped deliberately, add -Djacoco.skip=true: that switches off this check together with the agents, the merge, the report and the floor, so no coverage claim is made from partial data. If no tier was skipped, a forked JVM died before writing its data - read the Surefire or Failsafe output above.

requireFilesSize.message: Every coverage execution data file must be present AND non-empty, and this rule reports both shapes because it cannot tell them apart. An absent file means a tier did not run, and the rule above names it. A file that is present but zero bytes is the more dangerous shape: it merges to nothing while looking like data, so the coverage report silently omits a whole tier and the floor check passes on what is left. That is what a forked JVM leaves when it dies before the agent flushes, and the Surefire or Failsafe output above will name the fork. Do not delete the file to get past this - rerun the tier.
